checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, accessory apartment or in-law provision
Only one principal building and its accessory structures per lot (575-412A)
Added living space may go only in the principal building, not in an unattached accessory structure (575-610A(4))

Converting a single-family house into a two-family dwelling is permitted where two-family dwellings are permitted by right: R-2, R-3 and CC. Each unit needs at least 900 sq ft (575-610A(3), 575-411, use table)
R-1 does not allow two-family dwellings. R-3 allows conversion to multifamily (up to four units) by special exception (use table, 575-610A)
A tiny home (500 to 750 sq ft) is a principal dwelling, allowed by right only in R-3, not a second unit on a house lot (575-202, 575-610N)
Unattached residential accessory buildings: side and rear 10 ft, front 20 ft, 15 ft high, two per lot, 1,600 sq ft each at most (575-402)
Where doubt exists, the language is read in favor of the property owner (575-104B)

R-1 conversion: 575-610A(3) permits converting a house to two units where 'the single-family dwelling or two-family dwelling is a use permitted by right'. Single-family is by right in R-1, so the words are open, but two-family is not permitted in R-1. The file reads R-1 as not allowed. Ask the zoning officer
Parking: 2 spaces per dwelling unit for single-family and two-family dwellings (575-801C)

status.note: The code has no ADU text. The use table lists single-family, two-family and multifamily dwelling units, conversions and tiny homes, but no accessory unit.

path.note: 'there shall be no more than one principal building and its permitted accessory structures located on each lot'. No section sends unlisted uses to a hearing. A second unit that is not a two-family conversion needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

fallback_path.note: A lot that fails a district rule also needs a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Permitted where two-family dwellings are permitted by right. Each unit at least 900 sq ft. No exterior stair on the front and no parking in the front yard if it becomes multifamily. 2 parking spaces per unit. District lot 7,500 sq ft, 75 ft wide, but an existing lot of record below it may still be built on if setbacks, height and coverage are met (575-709A). A twin (one side of a semidetached pair) split into two units makes a three-unit building, which is multifamily, a special exception in R-2.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Each unit at least 900 sq ft. 2 parking spaces per unit. District lot 6,500 sq ft, 65 ft wide, but an existing lot of record below it may still be built on if setbacks, height and coverage are met (575-709A). A twin split into two units makes a three-unit building (multifamily, permitted in R-3).

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Each unit at least 900 sq ft. 2 parking spaces per unit. District lot 4,500 sq ft, but an existing lot of record below it may still be built on (575-709A). A twin split into two units makes a three-unit building (multifamily, special exception in CC).

value.name: Conversion to multifamily (three or four units)
value.conditions: At most four units per lot, each at least 750 sq ft. No exterior stair on the front, no parking in the front yard. 35 ft setback next to an existing single-family dwelling. 12 units per net acre at most.

alternatives.note: Not ADUs. Use table: 'Two-Family Dwelling Unit' N P P P for R-1, R-2, R-3, CC. 'Conversion to Multi-Family' S in R-3 only. 610A(3): 'the conversion of a single-family dwelling unit into a two-family dwelling unit is permitted, provided that the single-family dwelling or two-family dwelling is a use permitted by right in the zoning district'.

zoning_districts.note: No district lists an ADU. Reading of a silent code.

value.condition: 'The adding or construction of additional living space ... shall be limited to the principal structure or building on the property and shall not be placed in an unattached accessory structure.'
No more than one principal building and its accessory structures per lot.

A single-family or two-family dwelling unit needs at least 900 sq ft of habitable floor area. The section title says minimum, the table column reads 'Maximum Size Per Dwelling Unit'. Read as a minimum.

gates.note: Rules that reach any second unit.

historic_bypass.note: The historical overlay adds no residential use.

types_allowed.note: No ADU form is listed. Living space may not go in an unattached accessory structure (575-610A(4)).

max_height_ft.note: Accessory building rule, not an ADU rule. Unattached residential accessory buildings: 15 ft, two per lot, 1,600 sq ft each.

setback_side_ft.note: Residential unattached accessory building: 10 ft side.

setback_rear_ft.note: Residential unattached accessory building: 10 ft rear.

setback_front_ft.note: Only in a side or rear yard. 20 ft front setback in the table.

accessory_structure_max_sqft.note: 'Maximum Floor Area (square feet)' 1,600 for a residential unattached accessory building.

separation_ft.note: No distance between buildings for accessory buildings.

internal_uses_district_height.note: An attached accessory building is part of the principal building. District height 35 ft.

family_only.note: No ADU rule. A family allows up to four unrelated persons.

short_term_rental_banned.note: No ADU rule. Short-term home rental: not permitted in R-1, special exception in R-2, permitted in R-3 and CC.

max_adus.note: Reading: 0 means the code allows no ADU.

reading.value: No ADU row. Single-family and two-family dwelling units: 2 spaces each. A house converted to two units needs 4 in total.
